key_insight: In STEMI patients, a distinct gut microbiome pattern was associated with primary VT/VF, and a machine-learning model using acute-phase taxa showed promising discrimination.
clinical_relevance: If validated, stool microbiome signatures could support early risk stratification for malignant ventricular arrhythmias after STEMI.
method: 33 STEMI patients were sampled in the acute and recovery phases for full-length 16S rRNA sequencing.
An ML pipeline screened taxonomic features to find reproducible biomarkers linked to primary VT/VF.
Functional prediction analysis (PICRUSt2) was used to infer pathways and enzymes related to the microbiome signal.
evidence_signal: A reduced-feature SVM model achieved an AUROC of 0.846 with 85.7% sensitivity and 76.9% specificity in the study cohort.
watch_item: This was a small exploratory study, so the biomarkers and model need validation in larger independent cohorts before any clinical use.
paper_title: Machine Learning Approach to Identify Gut Microbiota Biomarkers in Patients with ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction Presenting Primary Ventricular Tachyarrhythmias
